content.title: Everything that happened on Day 1 at Augusta National
content.text: McIlroy shares 18-hole lead with BurnsRory McIlroy will head into the second round of the 2026 Masters with a share of the lead.Last year’s champion made a superb start to his title defence, carding a 5-under-par 67 to join Sam Burns at the top of the leaderboard. Patrick Reed, Jason Day and Kurt Kitayama make up the top five after 18 holes having all finished 3 under par.Scottie Scheffler started his round brilliantly with an eagle and a birdie in the first three holes, but then did not pick up another stroke in a 2-under 70.Jon Rahm arrived at this year’s Masters as one of favorites but endured a brutal time, finishing 6 over par. Fellow LIV golfer Bryson DeChambeau also struggled, carding a 4-over 76.Share your thoughts with us at live@theathletic.com. Want more Masters coverage? Sign up for our Golf Briefing newsletter here.WinnerPOSPLAYERTOTAL1Rory McIlroyNIR-12SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementSecond-round tee timesHere are the tee times for tomorrow's second round (all players will open on the first hole; all times are ET):7:40 a.m.: Samuel Stevens, Sungjae Im7:50 a.m.: Andrew Novak, Tom McKibbin, Brian Campbell8:02 a.m.: Mike Weir, Wyndham Clark, Mateo Pulcini (a)8:14 a.m.: Zach Johnson, Michael Kim, Nicolai Højgaard8:26 a.m.: Danny Willett, Davis Riley, Ethan Fang (A)8:38 a.m.: Adam Scott, Daniel Berger, Brian Harman8:50 a.m.: Fred Couples, Min Woo Lee, Fifa Laopakdee (a)9:02 a.m.: Sergio Garcia, Aaron Rai, Jacob Bridgeman9:19 a.m.: Harry Hall, Corey Conners, Michael Brennan9:31 a.m.: J.J. Spaun, Maverick McNealy, Tyrrell Hatton9:43 a.m.: Jon Rahm, Chris Gotterup, Ludvig Åberg9:55 a.m.: Jordan Spieth, Justin Rose, Brooks Koepka10:07 a.m.: Sepp Straka, Ben Griffin, Justin Thomas10:19 a.m.: Scottie Scheffler, Robert MacIntyre, Gary Woodland10:31 a.m.: Harris English, Marco Penge, Si Woo Kim10:51 a.m.: John Keefer, Haotong Li11:03 a.m.: Naoyuki Kataoka, Max Homa, Carlos Ortiz11:15 a.m.: José María Olazábal, Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen, Aldrich Potgieter11:27 a.m.: Angel Cabrera, Sami Valimaki, Jackson Herrington (a)11:39 a.m.: Charl Schwartzel, Max Greyserman, Ryan Fox11:51 a.m.: Vijay Singh, Matt McCarty, Rasmus Højgaard12:03 p.m.: Kurt Kitayama, Kristoffer Reitan, Casey Jarvis12:15 p.m.: Bubba Watson, Nicolas Echavarria, Brandon Holtz (a)12:32 p.m.: Cameron Smith, Sam Burns, Jake Knapp12:44 p.m.: Keegan Bradley, Ryan Gerard, Nick Taylor12:56 p.m.: Dustin Johnson, Shane Lowry, Jason Day1:08 p.m.: Patrick Reed, Tommy Fleetwood, Akshay Bhatia1:20 p.m.: Bryson DeChambeau, Matt Fitzpatrick, Xander Schauffele1:32 p.m.: Hideki Matsuyama, Collin Morikawa, Russell Henley1:44 p.m.: Rory McIlroy, Cameron Young, Mason Howell (a)1:56 p.m.: Viktor Hovland, Patrick Cantlay, Alex NorenScheffler's first-round charge stalled Getty ImagesMan, it looked like it was going to be a monster day for Scottie Scheffler at Augusta National. The world’s top-ranked golfer has won two of the last four Masters, and he made the leaderboard tremble by sinking an eagle putt at the par-5 second and then driving the green at the 350-yard third for a two-putt birdie.If you win three green jackets in five years, that counts as a dynasty, right?Right?But as the afternoon got longer and the golf course got firmer and the winds got trickier, Scheffler’s charge stalled, and he ultimately settled for a 2-under 70, three strokes off the lead shared by Rory McIlroy and Sam Burns.Scheffler was asked afterward about his longer-than-usual pre-Masters layoff, which he deemed necessary for good cause: to be present for the birth of his second son, Remy. Scheffler’s last start came at last month’s Players Championship.“Typically, I play Houston before this tournament,” he said, “so it was a little bit of a different prep than I’m used to. …For good reason. Actually, I committed thinking the baby might come a little bit early, but I was glad I stayed home because I think that Friday, so was definitely glad that I wasn’t out of town and I was able to be home for that.“It was good to get home and take my mind off tournament golf for a little bit and get to practice, prepare, and play at home. …It was a sweet time.”Scheffler said he wished he could have made some noise on the back-nine par-5s (he parred both), though conditions made No. 15 a more brutal test than usual (his playing partner Robert MacIntyre made an ungodly quadruple-bogey 9).“I felt like I hit it nice today,” the betting favorite said. “Was in the fairway a lot. Hit a lot of nice iron shots. … Overall, I thought it was a really solid day.”Meet the new Rory McIlroySo much for the idea that a laid-back Rory McIlroy, the Masters and Grand Slam weights finally off his back, would simply go through the motions at Augusta and enjoy one last victory tour after last year’s cathartic victory.It sure looked like that at times. Fresh off refusing to speak to playing partner Bryson DeChambeau during his final round in last year’s tournament, McIlroy cut loose today, talking, joking and dispensing advice to teenage U.S. Amateur winner Mason Howell. And yet, McIlroy still shot a 67 to take a share of the clubhouse lead heading into round two.Ian O’Connor watched a new version of McIlroy emerge at Augusta National today, and writes that this Rory may be even more dangerous than the driven, burdened figure he was up until last year.Oh, and more from Ian on McIlroy’s closest peer, Scottie Scheffler, in a few minutes...Tough stretch hurts Åberg Ludvig Åberg had something going today with three birdies in the first six holes. But two bogeys and two double bogeys in a five-hole stretch derailed Åberg’s round.In his third Masters appearance, he finished at 2-over 74.💬 “I left myself in tricky spots, which is the mistake from the first place. Shouldn't be long right of 9. Shouldn't be long left of 13. So naturally, I kind of put myself in a tricky spot. And then 9, you know, the last thing you want to do is kind of leave it up there. So I hit it a little bit too firm, and it kind of hit the downslope and three-putt from there.“And, first off, I shouldn't be in those situations where I have those shots in front of me.”Some good and bad for Scott Adam Scott’s round included an eagle and three birdies. That was the good. The bad? The five bogeys. Still, at even-par 72, the 2013 Masters winner is only five shots off the lead.💬 “It's not easy out there. Though the wind is not blowing hard, it was moving around. I felt like on several shots today, every time I was committing to a shot, the wind felt like it moved around, so it made it very hard to start again and recommit.“It's tricky because on some of the shots it's like if you make the wrong choice it starts … you're figuring out how to not have a disaster happen. That's how this course is.”Playing in the tournament for the 25th year, Scott has been at par or better after the first round 13 times.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementDisappointing finish for Smith Cameron Smith kind of fought his game throughout the first round today at the Masters, but he finally fought back to even par at No. 16 with a chip-in birdie.That momentum didn’t last long, however, as he finished with two bogeys for a 2-over 74. 💬 “I kind of scratched it around today. Wasn't my best stuff for sure, and it was nice to see that one go in. I was kind of thinking, ‘All right, could be away here with the putt around.’ Hit a great drive down 17, and, yeah, just hit it over the back there where you can't. Hit a half-decent shot, actually.“So couple of quick fives just like that. This place can do it to you.”Couples' collapse Fred Couples was at 2 under through 14 holes, and you could almost hear the murmurs and whispers around Augusta National. But then the 66-year-old former Masters winner went 8 over in a three-hole stretch with his round crumbling around him.It started with his third shot on No. 15, rolling back into the water, and it resulted in a quadruple bogey 9. 💬 “I was cruising along and making a few putts when I needed to. Then I actually had a perfect yardage, and I had seen a couple other guys, not in my group, but skip it over that green. I just felt like, you know, it was a shot I can handle.“I just kind of skinned it off the downhill lie and didn't carry far enough. Then I did the same thing.”Couples followed that with double bogeys on No. 16, with another ball in the water, and on No. 17 and finished his round at 6-over 78.💬 “Then on 16, I tried to regroup and just hit it down in the flat where the ball is going to roll anyway, and I pulled it and hit in the bank and went in the water. Then it just came … all the gas was gone. It was kind of a sour game, but it was fun.”Rose right back in the Masters mix Getty Images Justin Rose is officially the man who will not fade. Once again, at 45 years old, he’s right in the mix at a major championship.And if anything, he’s disappointed.He left the 16th hole 4-under par, one shot behind the lead, before two bogeys on 17 and 18 knocked him back a smidge, but that is not the point here. Rose did what he seems to always do these days. In the toughest of tests, he played smart, controlled golf and beat everybody in the details.Tuesday, I noticed Rose practicing around the chipping green so much longer than anybody else. While others played practice rounds or hit more balls on the range, Rose spent at least an hour practicing different quirky pitches over bunkers and off awkward slopes. So on 13, with 91 yards to the tricky pin, he hit a perfect pitch to three feet for birdie.On the ever-difficult 15, he hit a 226-yard iron shot that perfectly settled into the back of the green — something few players achieved — and easily two-putted for birdie. That shot alone gained him 0.80 strokes compared to the field on 15, which for reference is a lot.When he finished T6 at the 2024 PGA Championship, he said he might be in the “Indian summer” of his career. He was right, because it launched the Rose-aissance. He nearly won the 2024 Open Championship despite playing in the harder wave against horrific conditions. He took Rory McIlroy to a playoff at last year’s Masters. And in February, he won the Farmers Insurance Open.Nobody is taking Justin Rose lightly any more.Another good start for Rose Justin Rose knows what it takes to play well in the first round of the Masters. And he showed it off again today at Augusta National.Playing in the Masters for the 21st time, Rose fired his 12th under-par opening round.The three-time runner-up, including last year, finished at 2-under 70, even with bogeys on the final two holes.💬 “Overall, it’s a good start. Just big-picture, I kind of knew the course was going to be playing tricky today, especially this afternoon. Yesterday was quite a windy day. This morning was cold. I thought it was going to take a lot of the moisture out of the golf course.“Obviously, it was a beautiful afternoon. The wind laid down a little bit. It was nice to play out there. Obviously, my day, yeah, spoiled a little bit by two late bogeys, but other than that, I think a good start to the tournament.”Big names on top There are 16 players under par after the first round of the Masters, and some of the biggest names in golf are in that group.Eight of those players are major championship winners, including co-leader and defending Masters champion Rory McIlroy.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFamiliar feeling for McIlroy Rory McIlroy made history last April at Augusta National. He finally won the Masters, and he became just the sixth player to complete the career Grand Slam. So did he feel any different today on the 1st tee for this year’s Masters first round?💬 “I was nervous, I was anxious just like I always am on that 1st tee. It's the first round of the major season, the first round of the 16 most important rounds of the year. I'm thankful that I felt the same as I always have. I think it would be worrisome if I didn't feel that way because it definitely still means something to me.”McIlroy started slowly with one birdie and one bogey in the first seven holes. A birdie on No. 8 gave his round a spark, and he also birdied Nos. 9, 13, 14 and 15 with no other bogeys.He hit only 5 of 14 fairways but hit 13 of 18 greens in regulation.💬 “I would say that I didn't hit the ball very well the first seven holes, and sometimes here that would lead me to get tentative and a little guidy, and I kept swinging, just trusting that I'm going to find it eventually. So maybe that was a little bit different.”More on Burns’ round Sam Burns shared some more thoughts on his play today, shooting a 5-under 67. That’s his best round at Augusta National:💬 “I think I drove it really nice. That obviously helps. Then just tried to get the ball on the green as much as possible.“You know, as you know, it's difficult to chip around these greens, and so really just trying to give myself as many opportunities as possible today.”Burns was 4 under on the par-5s with an eagle on No. 2 and birdies on Nos. 13 and 15.💬 “I think historically people who have success here play the par-5s really well, and we were able to do that today. So it's a good recipe around this golf course.”Woodland on his round Getty ImagesGary Woodland’s round today at the Masters kind of epitomized the late wave of players: a good, solid start with a little bit of struggle in the middle and then a grind on the second nine.Woodland, who has never finished in the top 10 at the Masters in 12 appearances, was 3 under through eight holes. But a bogey on No. 10 slowed his momentum, and he had pars the rest of the way, except for a bogey on No. 15.He finished at 1 under.💬 “I told Butch (Harmon) when we finished there, I thought I played better than that. The golf course firmed up. That back nine, there was some shots that we thought were pretty good that took off on us.“I’m fortunate I drove the ball great today and had the putter really rolling, which was nice. I felt like I hit some better iron shots that I didn't get enough out of. Overall, I’m happy where I'm at.”Great separated from good on the 15th hole Getty Images This was supposed to be one of the easier holes on the course. No. 15? That’s usually the second-lowest scoring at Augusta National. Par five. Five-hundred fifty yards. Downhill approach. Easy? Of course not. Nothing at ANGC is. But this is a scoring hole.So why was Robert MacIntyre giving the bird to the 15th green Thursday?Because Augusta National was hard. Firm and fast. A Masters week without any weather concerns, a rarity in recent years. And the grounds crew is letting it bake. Drives are going further, sure, but balls are bouncing off greens. Good luck controlling your spin. Which provides a sneaky beauty: Players are close enough to go for the green, but landing a long club is nearly impossible.💬 “The greens are like concrete,” Fred Couples said. “The course was really, really good.”MacIntyre held up the middle finger after hitting his second shot into the water in front of 15 green. But that wasn’t even the worst part! When he hit a shorter drop from 81 yards out on the downhill slope, he overspun his pitch and rolled it back into the water again. Then, he dropped in the same exact spot and this time it bounced off the back of the green for an 18-yard pitch.And he wasn’t the lone quadruple we saw. Couples entered the 15th hole 2-under at the time. From a similar spot on the downslope, he hit two more in the water to drop to 2-over.Or there was Patrick Reed, near the lead at the time, who bounced an approach so hard off the green it went into the water by 16. He bogeyed.💬 “You fly it a little far, goes over the green. Fly it a little short, you come up short and the chipping is hard. For the really good players I think they want it like this. I know the Jon Rahms and Schefflers and Spieths and Rorys.”Couples is right. Per DataGolf, higher-skilled players separated themselves from lesser-skilled players roughly 24 percent more than an average PGA Tour stop on Sunday, and much more than even a normal Masters round.Let's hear from Scottie Scheffler Getty Images 💬 “The greens got really firm. You look at a hole like 12, that green’s typically a little bit softer, so you’re able to hold it. And today, especially late in the day, it was really challenging. And then you look at a hole like 15, you had to land it a yard or two onto the green in order to hold that green, which coming in with a 6 or 7 iron, that’s a big risk. “I did a good job of staying patient, playing smart, and trying to take advantage of the new opportunities that I had. I felt like I hit some really good putts late in the day, some that looked like they could have gone in but didn’t. But overall, definitely pretty proud of the effort today.”Scheffler said there was not really any impact from not playing competitive golf over the last few weeks as he and his wife welcomed the birth of their second son, crediting his solo preparation and playing with fellow pros Jordan Spieth and Si Woo Kim — along with some of his friends.💬 “I feel like I give my buddies so many strokes at home, I think that’s some high competition as well!” More coming on that treacherous 15th hole from my colleague Brody Miller in a moment...SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementThrilling finish for Bridgeman Masters rookie Jacob Bridgeman had a quiet first round going today … until the 18th hole.Bridgeman, the current FedEx Cup points leader, was at even par and hit his approach shot on the final hole over the back of the green. But he chipped in from there for a birdie to finish the day at 1 under.💬 “That was cool. I didn't have a whole lot of highlights today. Feel like I played pretty boring golf, which sometimes is good. I wanted something, and that was pretty special. Long of that green is a bad spot, and I hit an awesome shot.”Bridgeman had bogeys on the fifth and 14th holes and added birdies on the 13th and 16th. Other than that, his day was filled with pars and some solid play, hitting 12 of 14 fairways and 15 of 18 greens.💬 “I thought it was pretty much exactly what I had planned. I wanted to play conservative, figure out the course the best I could in tournament conditions, which it's very hard. It's pretty fast, and the greens are getting firm.“I didn't want to take many risks. I thought if I could play as conservative as I could, I could post a pretty good score and not let the scores get away from me.”Couples on Masters greens Getty Images Fred Couples has played the Masters a time or two (41 times, actually) and so his opinion on the current state of the greens at Augusta National should not be ignored:💬 “It's really rock hard.”A complaint? Not at all. 💬 “It's Augusta National. It's supposed to be like that.”Holtz soaking it in Mid-Am champion Brandon Holtz, who shot 81 in his Masters debut this morning is taking in everything the tournament has to offer: After his round, Holtz changed into khaki shorts and ordered himself a whiskey on the rocks.At about 3:30 p.m. on Thursday, the former college basketball player and current real estate agent stood adjacent to the oak tree with 10 of his family members and friends, rehashing the round and enjoying the Augusta National patron experience. Holtz, 39, is 14 years older than any of the other amateurs in the Masters field.He told The Athletic that he didn’t even hit the ball that poorly out there, despite the score being higher than he would have hoped for. The speed of Augusta National’s greens is what held Holtz back on Thursday. He said he had trouble adjusting his pace, constantly finding himself with uphill, downhill or sidehill putts, and he just couldn’t seem to find a feel.Holtz’s kids, who are six and two years old, are in town with him, but didn’t attend the tournament for their dad’s opening round. But Holtz’s father — who is 65 years old and is apparently about a 5 handicap — got to watch up close. He’s caddying for his son this week.Scheffler cards a 2-under-par 70 Getty ImagesScottie Scheffler and Gary Woodland each find the fairway bunker on 18. Scheffler’s approach gets on the front of the green, while Woodland’s falls short. Robert MacIntyre finds the greenside bunker on his second shot, then atones with a great chip to get his ball pin-high and set up a solid par — not that it will bring him much consolation as he heads to the clubhouse after shooting a miserable 80.Woodland also chips his shot near the hole, setting up a short par make to finish with a very solid first-round 71. Nice up-and-downs for both he and Scheffler, meanwhile has one of his best putts of the day on 18, weaving a 50-footer through elevation to set up a 4-foot par puttt. He sticks it. For his lack of lengthy putt makes today, he also did not have really any egregious misses either.That’s an opening-round 70 for the World No. 1, leaving him three strokes off the lead.
